bull.b: Sustained ~75.8% gross margins indicate attractive product-level economics for neffy, supporting durable unit profitability as volumes scale. High margins provide room to absorb commercial investments while improving the path to operating leverage if refill and penetration rates continue to grow.

Triple-year prescriptions, a growing installed base (~120k patients) and a built-out 148-rep field team show durable distribution and physician adoption. Repeat prescribers (~50%) and DTC/school programs create structural demand that should convert to stable refill revenue over the next 2–6 months.

Removal of the FDA age limit plus Health Canada and EU approvals materially expand addressable markets and enable partner-led launches. These regulatory wins create sustainable commercial runway and diversify revenue sources beyond the U.S., lowering single-market concentration risk.

bear.t: Large ongoing losses and cash burn
bear.b: Very large trailing losses and deeply negative operating cash flow mean persistent funding needs; reliance on current cash and future financing or rapid revenue scaling is critical. Continued high burn elevates dilution and execution risk if revenue cadence or payer wins slip.

Elevated SG&A to support the sales force and marketing compresses near-term margins and prolongs the path to profitability. If sales productivity or refill conversion underperforms, continued high operating spend could force deeper cuts or additional financing, undermining execution continuity.

Material prior-authorization barriers and ~22–23% abandonment reduce realized fills vs. written scripts, weakening revenue conversion and refill maturation. These structural access frictions limit sustainable uptake and make revenue growth dependent on payer decisions and conversion initiatives.
